title: Broken gradient trajectories form a family of broken lines
statement_scope: Whole Proposition 2.2.3: for a compact smooth Riemannian manifold M with smooth h:M->R whose critical set is finite, and critical points x,y with h(x)<h(y), the projection map pi: gTraj_{x,y}->Traj_{x,y} exhibits gTraj_{x,y} as a Traj_{x,y}-family of broken lines in the sense of Definition 2.1.3.

context_spans.label: Definition 2.1.1 and Definition 2.1.3, including the S-family axioms
Section 2.2 gradient-flow setup, Definition 2.2.1, and Notation 2.2.2

standard_prerequisites: Directed homeomorphisms and topological S-families of broken lines, Definition 2.1.1 and Definition 2.1.3, author PDF p.7.
Broken gradient trajectories and the total space gTraj_{x,y}, Definition 2.2.1 and Notation 2.2.2, author PDF pp.9-10.
Compact-open topology on Traj_{x,y}; compactness of the interval [h(x),h(y)]; finite discrete critical set Crit(M).
difficulty_reason: author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H2 because Proposition 2.2.3 at author PDF p.10 constructs gTraj_{x,y} as the image of (pi x e): Traj_{x,y} x [h(x),h(y)] -> Traj_{x,y} x M and uses compactness, closedness/injectivity, fibrewise directedness, and the finite critical set Crit(M) to verify the family-of-broken-lines axioms; this is a non-routine research example construction rather than a routine definition check.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Construction and proof that broken gradient trajectories form a family of broken lines, converting compactness/closedness of the evaluation map and finiteness of Critical(M) into the two axioms of Definition 2.1.3.
